data: Skeleton entry for /fleet (PRD-012 v0.2 / Phase A scaffold). Builder + agency + first-flight per public sources. Specs and gallery TBD in later phases.

NASA’s 2018–2022 Mars seismometer mission. Detected over 1,300 marsquakes, mapped the planet’s internal structure for the first time, and confirmed the existence of a large molten core. Ended when dust accumulation on its solar panels finally starved its power.
First to detect marsquakes; first interplanetary launch from US West Coast
Confirmed water ice in Martian soil
Lost during landing in 1999; the failure led NASA to review its “faster, better, cheaper” approach
First successful Mars lander; biology experiments
Second US Mars surface lander (Utopia Planitia 1976-09-03). Twin of Viking 1 lander; ran biology, soil chemistry + meteorology until 1980

First dedicated planetary seismograph on Mars. Detected over 1,300 marsquakes including a record magnitude-4.7 quake (S1222a) in May 2022. Heat-flow probe (HP³) failed to penetrate the unexpectedly cohesive regolith. Mission ended December 2022 when dust accumulation on solar panels dropped power below operating threshold.
